summary: Seiji Nemoto works in Buddhist studies, history and archaeology, and Japanology. He studied at Meiji University and served as a professor at the University of Tsukuba from around 1998 to 2014.
Seijun Ishii is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Komazawa University from around 1977 to 1986. He held a post as professor at Komazawa University around 1996.

Seiko Hirata was a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied at Kyoto University (~1947–1950) and under Shin'ichi Hisamatsu (~1948–1951), and held a post at Hanazono University from around 1970 to 1994.

Seiren Matsunami specialized in Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Tokyo under Naoshiro Tsuji (~1927–1930) and under Walther Schubring (~1936–1938). He held posts at Kyushu University (~1950–1966), Rissho University (~1966–1974), and Taisho University (attested 1972).

Seishi Karashima was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Sinology. He studied at the University of Tokyo, University of Cambridge, and Peking University, working under multiple supervisors. He held posts at Toho Gakuin, IRIAB, and Soka University (~1998–2019).
Seishin Kato was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Toyo University from around 1893 to 1899. He later held posts at Toyo University (~1904–1926) and Taisho University (~1926–1943).
Seitatsu Matsunami is an Indology and Tibetology scholar. He served as an assistant at the University of Tokyo and as a professor at Taisho University (attested 1992).
Seitetsu Moriyama specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He held posts at Bukkyo University, including as a professor in 2002, with further affiliations attested in 2004 and 2013.

Seizan Yanagida was a Buddhist studies and Sinology scholar. He studied at Hanazono University (~1942–1948) and later held posts at Hanazono University (~1960–1976), Kyoto University (attested 1986–1988), and Chubu University (~1986–1992).
Sen Wang was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Peking University from around 1931 to 1936 and served as a professor at Minzu University of China from around 1952 to 1988.

Senarat Wijayasundara is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. In 1999, he was attested as a teacher at the University of Kelaniya and as a visiting lecturer at the Buddhist and Pali College of Singapore.

Senchu Murano was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Rissho University (~1929–1933) and the University of Washington (~1934–1938). He later served as a professor at Rissho University from around 1953 to 1978.

Sengaku Maeda specialized in Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Tokyo and University of Pennsylvania. His appointments included the University of Pennsylvania, Gakushuin University, University of Tokyo (1973–1991), and Musashino University (~1991–2001).
Senkei Sakawa is a Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Rissho University until around 1965 and served there as a professor in the Department of Buddhism, attested between 1981 and 1985.

Senmyo Naniwa specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed a PhD at Savitribai Phule Pune University and was attested in 2005 as a researcher at the Eastern Institute and a professor at Bukkyo University.
Sensho Hibi is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology. He studied at Rissho University from around 1951 to 1959 and served there as an assistant professor from around 1968 to 1976.
Sensho Kimura is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Otani University from around 1962 to 1971. He later served as a professor at Otani University from around 1980 to 2008.

Sensho Murakami was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at Toyo University. He held posts at Sendan-Rin School, Toyo University, Otani University, and the University of Tokyo, where he was a professor from 1917 to 1922.

Seok-hyeong Kim is a religious studies and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Taisho University and held appointments as a part-time lecturer at Seoul National University and as a professor at Dongguk University.

Sergey Oldenburg was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Ivan Minayev at St. Petersburg University. He held posts at Saint Petersburg State University, the Russian Academy of Sciences, Asiatic Museum, and the Institute of Oriental Studies.
